subject: Renewal: Reserved GPU Pool Expansion + Isolation Confirmation
messages:

Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — additional reserved GPUs + isolation questions

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. As we discussed with the procurement team, Acme Health is prepared to move forward on renewal but we need two things confirmed before procurement will sign: (1) reserved capacity increase to support our new inference batch (estimate: +40 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved across two pools) and (2) strong tenant separation guarantees — we cannot share pools with other tenants and need logical/ network isolation and audit evidence.

Can you outline how Redwood will provision isolated reserved pools, what isolation controls are provided (network, compute fencing, KV cache isolation), and any SLA/throughput commitments we can include in the contract (p95 latency target, baseline tokens/sec)? Procurement also asked for the SOW and a network diagram to validate with our security team.

Appreciate a clear plan and timeline; Lydia from procurement (cc'ed) will lead legal/PO on our side.

Thanks,
Carlos
Senior AI Platform Manager
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — additional reserved GPUs + isolation questions

Hi Carlos / Lydia — thanks for the clear ask. High level answer here and I'll follow up with a technical note (Rishi) and an updated SOW for signature.

1) Capacity: Redwood can reserve an additional 40 A100-equivalent GPU slots for Acme. We'll split these into two dedicated pools (Pool-A for clinical inference, Pool-B for batch analytics) to match your traffic patterns. The term change to the renewal would be a 24-month reserved capacity commitment (pricing detail below).

2) Isolation: Reserved pools are logically isolated with the following controls: dedicated node allocation (no co-tenancy on assigned logical nodes), VLAN-level network segmentation for VPC/private deployments, tenant-aware KV cache namespaces, and RBAC at the model-routing layer. We will provide a network-segmentation diagram and an isolation checklist to satisfy your security review.

3) Throughput / SLOs: We can offer a contractual target of p95 token latency < 150ms for interactive requests (up to 2k tokens) and a baseline throughput guarantee of 1.2M tokens/min per pool during business hours, with agreed spike/burst allowances. If you need stricter p95 we can add a latency SLO with credits; I'll route options through Marissa.

Next steps: Marcus will draft the updated SOW and pricing; Rishi will send a technical appendix describing isolation controls and audit evidence we can share (SOC2 excerpts, audit logs retention). Once legal signs off we'll push a DocuSign for the renewal + amendment. Timeline: draft SOW by 7/17, technical appendix by 7/18, final contract ready for signature by 7/20.

Does that timeline work on your side?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales — East
Redwood Inference

Carlos — looping in more specifics from the capacity planning side.

We recommend the following split given your usage profile: Pool-A (real-time clinical, 24 GPUs A100-eq, pinned to low-latency routing with KV cache warm-up), Pool-B (batch analytics, 16 GPUs A100-eq, configured for throughput with multi-request batching). We'll provision node pools in two AZs for HA; node fencing ensures no other tenant will be scheduled onto those reserved nodes. Operational notes:
- Autoscaling: reserved capacity is guaranteed; we can configure burst capacity for short windows but charge reconciliation applies.
- Cache isolation: separate namespace + strict eviction policies so dataset/keyspace collisions are impossible.
- Monitoring: you'll get per-pool dashboards and per-route token/latency breakdowns in Redwood Console.

I'll attach the draft SOW and an ops playbook for migration. If procurement needs an explicit statement about physical separation (we do not offer physically segmented racks in our hosted stack by default) we can put language that reserved nodes will not host other tenants' workloads and include audit logs as proof.

-Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_Acme_Reserved_Pool_v3.pdf, redwood-dedicated-appendix.docx

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acmehealth.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Technical appendix: isolation controls and audit artifacts (for Acme security)

Carlos / Lydia — a few technical details your security team asked for in the questionnaire:

- Node fencing: Reserved pools are implemented as tagged node groups in the orchestration layer. Scheduler-level affinitized placement prevents non-tagged workloads from being placed on reserved node groups. We can provide placement logs for a defined window (eg last 90 days) as audit evidence.
- Network: For Private/VPC mode we'll provision dedicated subnets with ACLs and security group rules, and provide a network-segmentation diagram (attached). For hosted mode, logical VLANs and tenant egress IP controls are used.
- KV cache + model artifacts: Namespaced KV caches per tenant; model artifacts for Acme will be stored under a tenant-specific path with access controls. We can provide SHA-256 hashes and signed manifests for models to prove no tampering.
- Logging & retention: Audit trail for scheduling, model loading, and network changes retained for 1 year by default (extendable). Logs are available via S3 export or via a secured API endpoint for your SIEM.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 45-minute technical call with your security architects and our infra team to walk through the attached diagram and provide sample log extracts.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Infra Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachment: network-segmentation-diagram.png

Carlos / Lydia — thank you for the quick reviews. Per our timeline we've uploaded the amended SOW and the technical appendix to the DocuSign packet and shared the HubSpot deal. Summary of what is in the amendment: 

- Term: 24 months reserved commitment starting 2026-08-01
- Capacity: +40 A100-equivalent GPUs split into Pool-A (24 GPUs) and Pool-B (16 GPUs)
- Isolation guarantees: scheduler-level node fencing, VLAN/subnet segmentation, KV cache namespaces, separate model artifact paths, and audit log exports on request
- Throughput/SLO: p95 token latency target < 150ms (interactive), baseline 1.2M tokens/min per pool during business hours; latency-credit schedule included
- Pricing & credit: per-month reserved fee as in SOW_Acme_Reserved_Pool_v3.pdf; one-time migration uplift credit of $15k applied to first invoice

Please review and sign the DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/contract/rdw-acme-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9876543

If you want a technical walkthrough before signing, Rishi and Marcus are available tomorrow morning. Otherwise we'll prepare provisioning and aim to complete pool provisioning in the first maintenance window after signature (estimated 3–5 business days).

Thanks again — excited to keep Acme on Redwood.

Best,
Olga Petrov
